newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France Europe seen at breakeven in 1999-2000.
newsitem.headline: Air France Europe seen at breakeven in 1999-2000.

text.p: Air France Europe is expected to produce another loss in 1997-98 but should reach breakeven in 1999-2000, according to Air France Managing Director Patrice Durand.

He was commenting on the Air France subsidiary's results for 1996/97, which were released on Thursday and showed a net loss of 488 million francs ($84.9 million), after a year-earlier loss of 321 million.
Air France Europe merges fully with its parent this year. The absorption will be effective from September 30 but made retroactive for accounting purposes to April 1997.
"Air France Europe has already seen its low-point. We have a forecast over three years that, within the Air France group, the domestic sector (Air France Europe) will reach breakeven," Durand said.
"The contribution is set to be negative in 1997-98 and at breakeven in 1999-2000," he told reporters.
Restated under its parent company's consolidation standards the 1996/97 loss at Air France Europe comes in at 671 million francs, he said.
Air France Europe, formerly called Air Inter, has made a cumulative loss of 1.1 billion francs over the last two financial years and an aggregate operating loss of 1.3 billion.

Air France has been slated for privatisation by the current centre-right ruling coalition. The coalition parties are fighting for power in a parliamentary election runoff vote next Sunday after trailing to the left in the first round. ($ = 5.749 French Francs)
